questions.q: A retail partner must upload daily files by SFTP into S3. The partner's firewall team will only allow traffic to a fixed list of IP addresses. The company wants no servers to manage. Which design fits?

options.t: Transfer Family server with a VPC internet-facing endpoint and Elastic IPs
options.why: Right: Elastic IPs give fixed addresses the partner can allow-list, and security groups can limit partner CIDRs.

options.t: Transfer Family server with a public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: public endpoint IPs are AWS-managed and can change, so they cannot be allow-listed.

options.t: Transfer Family server with a VPC internal endpoint
options.why: Wrong: it has only private IPs and is reachable just from the VPC and connected networks, not the internet.

options.t: An SFTP server on EC2 behind a Route 53 record
options.why: Wrong: it works but means patching, HA and capacity work, which the company wants to avoid.

questions.explain: Fixed IPs for allow-lists mean a VPC internet-facing endpoint with Elastic IPs.
questions.remember: Partner needs a static IP to allow-list → Transfer Family VPC internet-facing endpoint with Elastic IPs. Public endpoint IPs can change.
variants: No internet exposure at all, only VPN or Direct Connect → VPC internal endpoint.
Simplest setup and no IP allow-list needed → public endpoint.
Restrict which partner networks may connect → security group CIDRs on the VPC endpoint.

questions.q: Partners authenticate to SFTP with passwords stored in Okta. The company wants to move to Transfer Family without changing how partners log in. Which identity provider option fits?

options.t: Service managed users
options.why: Wrong: service managed users use SSH public keys only, not passwords.

options.t: Custom identity provider using Lambda or API Gateway
options.why: Right: the function checks the password against Okta and returns the IAM role and home directory.

options.t: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory
options.why: Wrong: it is for users that live in AD, not in Okta.

options.t: An IAM user per partner
options.why: Wrong: Transfer Family does not authenticate SFTP users as IAM users.

questions.explain: Passwords from an external IdP such as Okta need a custom identity provider.
questions.remember: Password login against Okta, Entra ID, Cognito or a database → custom identity provider (Lambda or API Gateway + Lambda). Service managed is SSH keys only.
variants: Users live in corporate Active Directory → the Directory Service identity provider with group-to-role mapping.
A few partners using SSH keys → service managed users.
Lambda returns an empty response `{}` → the login is denied.

questions.q: A company has an on-premises SFTP server used by many partners. It wants to move to Transfer Family so partners change nothing: same hostname, no known_hosts warnings. Which two actions help? (Choose two.)

options.t: Import the existing SFTP host key into the Transfer Family server
options.why: Right: clients keep trusting the same server identity.

options.t: Point the existing DNS name at the Transfer Family endpoint, for example with Route 53
options.why: Right: partners keep using the same hostname.

options.t: Enable FTP on the server so old clients work
options.why: Wrong: FTP is unencrypted and does not address host keys or hostnames.

options.t: Ask every partner to reconfigure a new hostname
options.why: Wrong: it defeats the aim of no partner changes.

options.t: Switch to AS2
options.why: Wrong: AS2 is a B2B messaging protocol, not a drop-in for SFTP clients.

questions.explain: Import the old host key and keep the DNS name so partners see no change.
questions.remember: Migrating an SFTP host without partner changes → import the host key and repoint the DNS name to the Transfer endpoint.
variants: For FTPS the certificate must match the custom hostname.
If you do not import a key, AWS generates a new host key and clients see a changed identity.
A custom hostname can be a Route 53 alias or CNAME.

questions.q: A SaaS company gives each customer an SFTP login. Each customer must see only their own folder in one shared S3 bucket and must not see the bucket name. What is the best setup?

options.t: One shared IAM role with no restrictions and a note to customers
options.why: Wrong: customers could read each other's data.

options.t: A home directory per user with the Restricted option (or a session policy using `${transfer:UserName}`)
options.why: Right: the user is locked to their home folder and cannot see above it or the bucket name.

options.t: One bucket per customer with no further controls
options.why: Wrong: it isolates data but adds management work and still needs per-user access controls.

options.t: Public endpoint with security groups per customer
options.why: Wrong: public endpoints have no security groups and this does not isolate folders.

questions.explain: Home directory plus Restricted (chroot) or a session policy isolates users inside one bucket.
questions.remember: Each customer sees only their folder → home directory including the username plus Restricted or a session policy with policy variables. Logical directories hide the bucket structure.
variants: Present clean friendly paths like /inbox mapped to real prefixes → logical directories.
Large multi-tenant S3 access at scale → S3 Access Points or Access Grants.
Service managed users have a limit of 2,000 logical directory entries.

questions.q: Files arrive in S3 over SFTP and are PGP-encrypted. The company must decrypt them, tag them and send failures to quarantine, without running servers. Which solution is best?

options.t: A Transfer Family managed workflow with decrypt and tag steps and an exception-handling step
options.why: Right: workflows run after upload, with built-in decrypt, tag and copy steps plus exception handling.

options.t: A cron job on EC2 that polls the bucket
options.why: Wrong: it needs a server to manage and is slower.

options.t: DataSync task with a filter
options.why: Wrong: DataSync copies data in bulk and does not decrypt PGP files after SFTP upload.

options.t: A Transfer Family connector
options.why: Wrong: connectors send or pull files to and from remote SFTP servers; they do not decrypt uploads.

questions.explain: Post-upload decrypt, tag and copy are built-in managed workflow steps.
questions.remember: Process files after SFTP/FTPS/FTP upload (PGP decrypt, tag, copy, custom Lambda scan) → managed workflow with an exception path.
variants: Need more than 8 steps or complex orchestration → S3 events with Lambda, Step Functions or EventBridge.
Files uploaded over AS2 → workflows do not run for AS2 messages.
A zero-byte file is uploaded → the workflow does not start.

questions.q: A bank publishes statements on its own SFTP server. The company must fetch them nightly into S3 with no custom code, trusting only the bank's known server. Which solution fits?

options.t: Transfer Family SFTP connector with Secrets Manager credentials, a trusted host key and an EventBridge schedule
options.why: Right: the connector acts as the SFTP client, and the host key blocks man-in-the-middle servers.

options.t: A Transfer Family SFTP server
options.why: Wrong: a server accepts inbound connections from partners; it does not pull from a bank.

options.t: Transfer Family web app
options.why: Wrong: web apps give users a browser UI to S3 data.

options.t: AS2 agreement with the bank
options.why: Wrong: AS2 is for EDI messaging, and the bank offers SFTP.

questions.explain: To pull from a partner's SFTP server, use a connector, not a server.
questions.remember: Server = partners connect to you. Connector = you connect to partners (send or retrieve, credentials in Secrets Manager, trusted host keys, optional VPC egress).
variants: Static source IP needed for the bank's allow-list → connector with VPC egress through NAT.
Schedule the pull → EventBridge rule calling StartFileTransfer.
Partners push files to you → a server.

questions.q: A legacy system can speak only FTP. It must send files to S3, and the security team says nothing may be exposed to the internet. Which setup is correct?

options.t: FTP on a public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: FTP is not supported on a public endpoint and is unencrypted.

options.t: FTP on a VPC internal endpoint reached over the private network
options.why: Right: FTP is VPC only, and an internal endpoint keeps it off the internet.

options.t: FTPS on a public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: FTPS needs a VPC endpoint and an ACM certificate, and the legacy system speaks FTP only.

options.t: SFTP on a public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: the legacy system cannot speak SFTP.

questions.explain: FTP works only on VPC endpoints and is unencrypted, so keep it internal.
questions.remember: FTP → VPC only and unencrypted, use inside private networks. FTPS → VPC endpoint plus ACM certificate. Prefer SFTP when clients allow.
variants: Partners need encryption with FTP clients → FTPS with an ACM certificate matching the hostname.
FTP/FTPS connections fail on transfers → open data ports 8192-8200.
Clients can use SSH → SFTP on port 22.

questions.q: A trading partner in retail insists on exchanging EDI documents with signing, encryption and delivery receipts. The company wants the documents stored in EFS. What is the issue?

options.t: AS2 on Transfer Family meets the protocol need but supports only S3, not EFS
options.why: Right: AS2 gives signing, encryption and MDN receipts, but it is S3 only.

options.t: AS2 works with EFS, but only on a public endpoint
options.why: Wrong: AS2 does not support EFS on any endpoint.

options.t: SFTP satisfies the AS2 requirement unchanged
options.why: Wrong: the partner requires AS2 with MDN receipts.

options.t: Managed workflows will process AS2 files after upload
options.why: Wrong: AS2 messages do not run workflows.

questions.explain: AS2 means S3 only and no workflows; it adds signing, encryption and MDN receipts.
questions.remember: EDI or B2B with signed, encrypted messages and MDNs → AS2 (S3 only, no EFS, no workflows). SFTP, FTPS and FTP can use S3 or EFS.
variants: Need EFS with POSIX users → SFTP, FTPS or FTP, not AS2.
Business users want a browser to reach S3 → Transfer Family web apps with IAM Identity Center.
Bulk historic migration → DataSync, not Transfer Family.
